doc.title: Håkan Rydin interviewed by Monk Rowe, Glasgow, Scotland, July 27, 2016

title: How music grabbed him: playing by ear, his mother's records, starting jazz at 15
summary: Rydin has played piano all his life, learned by ear, heard Basie, Armstrong and Ellington via his mother, and began playing jazz at 15-16.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Well what steered you toward music in your youth?
What, when you were young, how did music grab you?

First of all I’ve been playing piano all my life. So I have memories as a little child playing by ear the children’s songs. And play by ear, that’s what I still do. So my mother listened to jazz, to Basie, Louis Armstrong, Ellington, those kind of things. So I got it by the record. I wouldn’t say I liked it very much, but I got it natural. I started playing jazz when I was maybe 15, 16. Before that I had some classical education. I played some pop, rock and blues, but when I was 15 or 16 I just started playing jazz, and it just came to me. I don’t feel it like a decision. It was just the natural thing to do.
